## Short answer

For most RVs, pick a station with a built-in 30A RV outlet and a high solar-input limit, then size the panels to that limit. Here are the combos I'd consider, from my search results.

### Best picks

| Use case | Power station | Key specs | Panel pairing |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Full-time boondocking / running the roof A/C** | EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 | 4,096Wh, 4,000W (8,000W surge), expandable past 12kWh, ~0-80% in 50 min on AC ([source](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)) | A large array. The older Delta Pro accepted up to 1,600W of solar ([source](https://outdoorpowerstations.com/articles/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti)). I didn't find the Pro 3's exact solar limit. |
| **Best value for big capacity** | ALLPOWERS R4000 | 3,456Wh LiFePO4, 3,600W at 120V, RV outlet, 2,000W solar input across three 650W inputs, 5-year warranty | Up to ~2,000W of panels, but you need panels on all three inputs to reach it |
| **Mid-range value** | BLUETTI AC200L | 2,048Wh, 2,400W, built-in 30A RV port, 1,200W solar input, ~62 lb ([source](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)) | Up to ~1,200W of panels |
| **Running A/C without a soft-start kit** | Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro | 3,024Wh, 3,000W (6,000W surge) ([source](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)) | Jackery SolarSaga panels |
| **Weekend trips** | Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 | 1,070Wh, 1,500W, 400W solar cap, ~23.8 lb | Two SolarSaga 200W panels use the full 400W input ([source](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)) |

### Where to buy

- **ALLPOWERS R4000:** [Buy at ALLPOWERS](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh). This is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you. The store price is $1,499. Code EXTRA12 takes $179.88 off for $1,319.12, but it applies only to orders over $1,200 and expires 2026-11-15. Checkout usually accepts one code per order. Returns are 30 days for unused items, you pay return shipping, and sale items may not be returnable. At 45 kg, it's a drop-it-in-a-bay unit, not a carry-around one. Details: [Dealectric listing](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh).
- **EcoFlow, Jackery, and Bluetti models:** My results had no direct product-page links for these, only articles with "check price" buttons. I'd rather not guess at URLs. You can find current prices through the [Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/) and [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/) comparisons, or on the manufacturers' sites.
- **Panels:** [NomadSignal](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife) suggests the Renogy 200W Foldable Solar Suitcase for smaller setups. Its page has no direct product link.

### How to choose

1. **Check the largest single load first.** A 13,500 BTU roof A/C draws about 1,500W running and spikes past 3,000W at startup. Stations under ~3,000W surge may struggle with it.
2. **Match panels to the solar-input limit.** Extra panels beyond the cap don't charge faster. The Jackery 1000 v2 tops out at 400W, and the older Bluetti AC200P at 700W.
3. **Capacity rule of thumb:** add up watts × hours. A 150W fridge over 10 hours is about 1,500Wh.
4. **Fixed roof panels vs. folding panels:** if you're parked in shade often, folding panels you can aim and move are worth the extra setup. For full-time use, a roof array saves effort.

### Caveats

- Most of these sources are affiliate sites, and prices and specs shift, so confirm them on the seller's page before buying.
- One source's pricing (e.g., the Delta Pro at $2,199) looks older than its "2026" label.
- The EmergencyEnergy article is written for Ontario, Canada. The specs apply, but its electrical-code notes don't. If you want to wire a station into your RV's inlet, have an electrician do it.

If you tell me your RV's A/C size, fridge type, and how many nights you boondock, I can narrow this to one station and a specific panel wattage.
